## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Hetuduka, Vedanāttika* is a text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It forms part of the extensive combinatory framework in which dyads (*duka*) are systematically correlated with triads (*tika*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Specifically, it represents the analytical section where the first dyad—the root dyad (*hetuduka*)—is cross-tabulated with the feeling triad (*vedanāttika*), proceeding through the standard permutation schemes that couple each dyad with all twenty-two triads of the Abhidhamma matrix [Nyanatiloka 2007].

No separate translations or external parallels in other canonical languages are recorded for this text by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Machine text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reflects the repetitive, formulaic nature of Abhidhamma exposition, identifying 130 matching passages distributed across 34 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its highest internal textual reuse is found in other *Paṭṭhāna* chapters treating the root dyad or the feeling triad—most significantly *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1), *Vedanāttika* (Patthana 1.3 and 13.2), *Hetuduka, Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 24.6), and parallel configurations of *Hetuduka, Vedanāttika* in other structural divisions (Patthana 9.2 and 15.2)—as well as sharing passages with the *Khandhavibhaṅga* of the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 1) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are recorded at or above the threshold score [DharmaNexus].
